arxiv-2210-14343.title: Enhanced mobility of dislocation network nodes and its effect on dislocation multiplication and strain hardening Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2210-14343.creator: N. Bertin, W. Cai, S. Aubry, A. Arsenlis, V.V. Bulatov
arxiv-2210-14343.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by N. Bertin, W. Cai, S. Aubry, A. Arsenlis, V.V. Bulatov. Understanding plastic deformation behavior of crystals in terms of the fundamental physics of dislocations has remained a grand challenge in computational materials science for decades. To overcome this challenge, method of Discrete Dislocation Dynamics (DDD) has been developed, with the premise that crystal plasticity should naturally emerge in its realistic complexity by letting a statistically representative ensemble of dislocations evolve in response to deformation.

arxiv-2311-07426.title: Optimising Human-AI Collaboration by Learning Convincing Explanations
arxiv-2311-07426.creator: Alex J. Chan, Alihan Hüyük, Mihaela van der Schaar
arxiv-2311-07426.description: Abstract Machine learning models are being increasingly deployed to take, or assist in taking, complicated and high-impact decisions, from quasi-autonomous vehicles to clinical decision support systems. This poses challenges, particularly when models have hard-to-detect failure modes and are able to take actions without oversight.

arxiv-2405-19537.title: Optimal complexity of parameterized quantum circuits
arxiv-2405-19537.creator: Guilherme Ilário Correr, Pedro C. Azado, Diogo O. Soares-Pinto, Gabriel Carlo
arxiv-2405-19537.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Guilherme Ilário Correr, Pedro C. Azado, Diogo O. Soares-Pinto, Gabriel Carlo. Parameterized quantum circuits play a key role for the development of quantum variational algorithms in the realm of the NISQ era. Knowing their actual capability of performing different kinds of tasks is then of the utmost importance. By comparing them with a prototypical class of universal random circuits we have found that their approach to the asymptotic complexity defined by the Haar measure is faster, needing less gates to reach it.

arxiv-2408-04466.title: One-Shot Method for Computing Generalized Winding Numbers
arxiv-2408-04466.creator: C. Martens and M. Bessmeltsev Université de Montréal, Canada
arxiv-2408-04466.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by C. Martens and M. Bessmeltsev Université de Montréal, Canada. The generalized winding number is an essential part of the geometry processing toolkit, allowing to quantify how much a given point is inside a surface, even when the surface has boundaries and noise. We propose a new universal method to compute a generalized winding number, based only on the surface boundary and the intersections of a single ray with the surface, supporting any oriented surface representations that support a ray intersection query.

arxiv-2508-03783.title: Probing and Enhancing the Robustness of GNN-based QEC Decoders with Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2508-03783.creator: Ryota Ikeda
arxiv-2508-03783.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as a powerful, data-driven approach for Quantum Error Correction (QEC) decoding, capable of learning complex noise characteristics directly from syndrome data. However, the robustness of these decoders against subtle, adversarial perturbations remains a critical open question.

arxiv-2511-06100.title: Differential inclusions and quasi-Lyapunov functions
arxiv-2511-06100.creator: Martin Ivanov, Mikhail Krastanov, Nadezhda Ribarska
arxiv-2511-06100.description: Abstract A sufficient condition for existence of a solution of a differential inclusion with a uniformly bounded right-hand side that has nonempty closed (possibly nonconvex) values is obtained. A new way to deal with the so-called “bad points” is proposed. An Olech-type result is obtained as a corollary.

arxiv-2602-24129.title: End-to-end Differentiable Calibration and Reconstruction for Optical Particle Detectors
arxiv-2602-24129.creator: Omar Alterkait, César Jesús-Valls, Ryo Matsumoto, Patrick de Perio, Kazuhiro Terao
arxiv-2602-24129.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Omar Alterkait, César Jesús-Valls, Ryo Matsumoto, Patrick de Perio, Kazuhiro Terao. Large-scale homogeneous detectors with optical readouts are widely used in particle detection, with Cherenkov and scintillator neutrino detectors as prominent examples. Analyses in experimental physics rely on high-fidelity simulators to translate sensor-level information into physical quantities of interest. This task critically depends on accurate calibration, which aligns simulation behavior with real detector data, and on tracking, which infers particle properties from optical signals.

pmc-10531018.description: Growing environmental concerns drive efforts to reduce packaging waste by adopting biodegradable polymers, coatings, and films.
